properties.name: A three-agent design trial is how reflow2 and flo2 are exercised on a real design concept: an OWNER, a DESIGNER and an OBSERVER, all AI agents. Each run is finished, its friction is triaged and fixed, and the trial is repeated on new concepts
properties.statement:
ANTHONY, 2026-09-29, verbatim: "I'd like to make sure we captured the idea that we ran were we had an owner, designer, and observer (all 3 being AI agents) design something...I think we learned a lot from this type of experiment and I'd like to finish (I think we only got through 3 steps of the ideal knowledge graph). I'd also like to do this concept in the future with other design concepts." The idea began mid-run on 2026-09-28: "You might need 2 agents to do this properly. One that interfaces with reflow2 and one that acts as the human user."

THE ROLES
- THE HUMAN states the brief and a few fixed answers at the start (where the design lives, scale, quality target, role), then delegates. The human is asked no design questions. Escalation is only for spending money or provisioning hardware; that was the owner's own rule in the first run.
- THE OWNER is a fresh agent context with NO design tools. It holds the brief and the human's fixed answers and decides by question number. It signs as "the owner", never as the human. It may read files and the web to judge a claim, and it writes nothing. It is told to accept what is sound, push back on weak reasons and unsupported numbers, and name the evidence it needs rather than guess.
- THE DESIGNER works the design through the SAME surface a real user would; for a hosted design, that is the claude.ai flo2 connector. It drafts, recommends and records the owner's word, quoted, with the owner linked. It settles nothing on its own. It keeps a FRICTION LOG as it goes: every refusal, workaround, missing tool or field, oversized reply, and act that took many calls, each with its rough cost in calls and characters.
- THE OBSERVER is the session that runs the trial. It spawns the other two, carries question batches and answers VERBATIM between them, and never decides. It keeps its own list of lessons and measures cost per round.

THE LOOP: the designer drafts and runs the gap check → a numbered batch of at most about 10 questions, each with options, a recommendation and a one-line reason → the owner answers by number → the designer records → repeat.

WHEN TO PAUSE: when the same tool friction repeats round over round, since more rounds would only re-measure it, or when what remains needs building or spending rather than deciding. At the pause, record the BASELINE:
- designer tool calls, minutes, and characters echoed against characters edited;
- owner calls and minutes per round;
- the questions still pending, stored in the design itself.

AFTER THE PAUSE:
1. The observer writes the lessons into the dev_reflow2 hub's docs/TRIAL-LOG.md and registers them as a field report in reflow2's design.
2. The report is triaged by skill (triage-feedback: root-cause on every issue, brainstorm on every idea).
3. The human says which ideas to promote.
4. The fixes ship.
5. The SAME design is resumed with FRESH agents on the fixed versions, as a before-and-after test against the baseline. A fresh owner must read its earlier decisions back from the design, which tests whether the design really carries the owner's word.
6. The design is FINISHED, and the trial repeats on a NEW concept.

FIRST RUN, as evidence (2026-09-28/29): "ideal knowledge graph", flo2 design 50f966697d6c5024, reflow2 0.74.0, 3 rounds, then paused (see that design's epoch:two-agent-rounds-1-to-3-then-paused-2026-09-29).
- The separate owner amended all four decisions the single agent had settled for itself. It caught a 2× sizing error against real exports, a Protocol Buffers pin with a fallback clause, and a stored closure that would have broken the memory budget.
- Triage changed 12 of the report's 30 conclusions and found 7 live recurrences (fact:the-2026-09-29-triage-changed-12-of-30-reported-conclusions-and-7-were-live-recurrences).
- The fix program is epoch:fix-what-the-two-agent-exercise-found-2026-09-29.

LIMITS, kept beside the rule:
- The owner is the same model family as the designer, so their blind spots are correlated. In the first run it caught errors of arithmetic, evidence and wording, not a wrong goal. It is no substitute for the human.
- Two agents agreeing can read like review when it is not.
- The observer's hand relay is the main cost until questions can be addressed to a person (req:a-question-is-addressed-to-a-person-and-records-who-answered).

HOW THIS SITS WITH EARLIER RECORDS:
- req:friction-has-a-baseline (dropped in dec:proposed-requirements-pruned) had the same shape: execution separated from evaluation, a blind evaluator, a stored baseline. It was dropped because "the answer to unconverted friction reports is to act on them, not to model them". This rule honours that ruling. It is a PRACTICE whose output is acted on (triage, then fixes, then a re-run), not a product mechanism that models friction.
- Whether reflow2 should SERVE a two-party mode as a skill stays open in dec:idea-a-designer-and-an-owner-work-a-design-as-two-parties. This rule is about running the trial, not about that feature.

ENFORCEMENT: not stated. This is a runbook, not a gate.
